content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — Section 21.1 cap basis is illusory.**

What I checked:
- **§21.1** — cap is expressly mutual and applies "regardless of the form of action" ✓
- **§21.2** — mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, with a helpful pro-Customer gloss making data restoration, replacement services, notices and incident response *direct* damages ✓
- **§21.3** — full preferred carve-out set (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP), plus confirmation that Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" ✓
- **§20** — Vendor indemnities are broad and sit outside the cap via the Excluded Claims definition ✓

The defect: the cap is measured by **"Fees"**, which §1.5 defines as the **Implementation Fee**, and §1.6 fixes that as a **one-time USD 12,000 charge stated in the first Order Form**. So the apparently reasonable "twelve months preceding" cap resolves to roughly USD 12,000 — well below even the walk-away threshold of six months' charges, and it ignores all subscription and later Order Form spend.

Redline (validated, ok:true): §21.1 cap basis becomes the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable by Customer under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and (b) USD 1,000,000 — a single-sentence edit that leaves mutuality, the damages exclusion and the carve-outs untouched. Fallback offered in the comment: a straight twelve months' charges cap measured across all Order Forms if the USD 1,000,000 floor is resisted.
